Summary: Jesus' confession command: whoever confesses him before men, him will he confess before his Father; whoever denies him, him will he deny.
Commandment: Whosoever therefore shall confess me before men, him will I confess also before my Father which is in heaven. But whosoever shall deny me before men, him will I also deny before my Father.
Application: Confession here is public allegiance under pressure, not private belief alone. The promise and the warning are joined: the confessor is owned, the denier disowned.
Purpose: Scripture's own reason: Christ will confess the confessor before his Father (Matthew 10:32).
Function: Private belief is not enough where public allegiance is demanded. A New Testament command, not a Mosaic one — the civil, ceremonial, and moral division does not sort it. Its goal was open confession under pressure: whoever confesses him before men, him will he confess before his Father. The evil it addressed was denial — hiding allegiance to Christ when naming him costs something. It restrained that evil by joining promise and warning: the confessor is owned before the Father, and the denier disowned.
